segments.speaker: PRESENTER
segments.en: This evening we’re delighted to welcome Dan Beagle, who’s just written a book on looking for and finding food in the wild.

segments.speaker: PRESENTER
segments.en: He’s going to tell us everything we need to know about picking wild mushrooms.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Thank you very much.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Well, I need to start by talking about safety.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: You really need to know what you’re doing because some mushrooms are extremely poisonous.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Having said that, once you know what to look for, it’s really worth doing for the amazing variety of mushrooms available – which you can’t get in the shops.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: But of course, you have to be very careful and that’s why I always say you should never consume mushrooms picked by friends or neighbours – always remember that some poisonous mushrooms look very similar to edible ones and it’s easy for people to get confused.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: The other thing to avoid is mushrooms growing beside busy roads for obvious reasons.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: But nothing beats the taste of freshly picked mushrooms – don’t forget that the ones in the shops are often several days old and past their best. /12 There are certain ideas about wild mushrooms that it’s important to be aware of.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Don’t listen to people who tell you that it’s only OK to eat mushrooms that are pale or dull – this is completely untrue.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Some edible mushrooms are bright red, for example.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Personally, I prefer mushrooms cooked but it won’t do you any harm to eat them uncooked in salads – it’s not necessary to peel them.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Another thing you should remember is that you can’t tell if a mushroom is safe to eat by its smell – some of the most deadly mushrooms have no smell and taste quite nice, apparently.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Finally, just because deer or squirrels eat a particular mushroom doesn’t mean that you can. /14 —– Of course, mushroom picking is associated with the countryside but if you haven’t got a car, your local park can be a great place to start.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: There are usually a range of habitats where mushrooms grow, such as playing fields and wooded areas.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: But you need to be there first thing in the morning, as there’s likely be a lot of competition – not just from people but wildlife too.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: The deer often get the best mushrooms in my local park.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: If you’re a complete beginner, I wouldn’t recommend going alone or relying on photos in a book, even the one I’ve written!

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: There are some really good phone apps for identifying mushrooms, but you can’t always rely on getting a good signal in the middle of a wood.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: If possible, you should go with a group led by an expert – you’ll stay safe and learn a lot that way.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Conservation is a really important consideration and you must follow a few basic rules.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: You should never pick all the mushrooms in one area – collect only enough for your own needs.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Be very careful that you don’t trample on young mushrooms or other plants.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: And make sure you don’t pick any mushrooms that are endangered and protected by law.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: There’s been a decline in some varieties of wild mushrooms in this part of the country.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Restaurants are becoming more interested in locally sourced food like wild mushrooms, but the biggest problem is that so many new houses have been built in this area in the last ten years.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: And more water is being taken from rivers and reservoirs because of this, and mushroom habitats have been destroyed.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Anyway, a word of advice on storing mushrooms.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Collect them in a brown paper bag and as soon as you get home, put them in the fridge.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: They’ll be fine for a couple of days, but it’s best to cook them as soon as possible – after washing them really carefully first, of course.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: So everybody knows what a mushroom tastes like, right?

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Well, you’ll be surprised by the huge variety of wild mushrooms there are.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: Be adventurous!

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: They’re great in so many dishes – stir fries, risottos, pasta.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: But just be aware that some people can react badly to certain varieties so it’s a good idea not to eat huge quantities to begin with.

segments.speaker: DAN
segments.en: OK, so now I’m going to show you ...

Questions 11-20
WILD MUSHROOMS
Choose TWO letters A–E.
Q Num: 11
Text: Which TWO warnings does Dan give about picking mushrooms?
Count: 2
Options:
    Id: A
    Text: Don't pick more than one variety at a time.
    Id: B
    Text: Don't pick mushrooms near busy roads.
    Id: C
    Text: Don't eat mushrooms given to you.
    Id: D
    Text: Don't eat mushrooms while picking them.
    Id: E
    Text: Don't pick old mushrooms.
Choose TWO letters A–E.
Q Num: 13
Text: Which TWO ideas about wild mushrooms does Dan say are correct?
Count: 2
Options:
    Id: A
    Text: Mushrooms should always be peeled before eating.
    Id: B
    Text: Mushrooms eaten by animals may be unsafe.
    Id: C
    Text: Cooking destroys toxins in mushrooms.
    Id: D
    Text: Brightly coloured mushrooms can be edible.
    Id: E
    Text: All poisonous mushrooms have a bad smell.
Choose the correct letter A, B or C.
Questions:
    Q Num: 15
    Text: What advice does Dan give about picking mushrooms in parks?
    Options:
        Choose wooded areas.
        Don't disturb wildlife.
        Get there early.
    Q Num: 16
    Text: Dan says it is a good idea for beginners to
    Options:
        use a mushroom app.
        join a group.
        take a reference book.
    Q Num: 17
    Text: What does Dan say is important for conservation?
    Options:
        selecting only fully grown mushrooms.
        picking a limited amount of mushrooms.
        avoiding areas where rare mushroom species grow.
    Q Num: 18
    Text: According to Dan, some varieties of wild mushrooms are in decline because there is
    Options:
        a huge demand for them from restaurants.
        a lack of rain in this part of the country.
        a rise in building developments locally.
    Q Num: 19
    Text: Dan says that when storing mushrooms, people should
    Options:
        keep them in the fridge for no more than two days.
        keep them in a brown bag in a dark room.
        leave them for a period after washing them.
    Q Num: 20
    Text: What does Dan say about trying new varieties of mushrooms?
    Options:
        Experiment with different recipes.
        Expect some to have a strong taste.
        Cook them for a long time.
